lines.meet: I'm Bakyt, sit down, there's tea. I walk first, because I read the ground, and you'll be fine if you step where I step.
lines.meet_neighbour: You're on the hills near my pasture, I think. I've seen you pass. Come and drink tea at my tent some evening.
lines.ask_home: Where are your people from? Tell me what country you walked when you were young.
lines.ask_work: What was your work, before? A man's work shows in how he walks.
lines.answer_home: The Tian Shan, in Kyrgyzstan, near Naryn. Six generations of my family walked the same route up to the high pasture.
lines.answer_work: Forty years a herder. Up to the summer grass in spring and down again in autumn, with an eagle on my arm.
lines.chat_food: Tea with milk and a little salt, and bread cooked in the ashes. A man can walk all day on that, and I have.
lines.chat_sleep: I sleep when it's dark and get up before the light. Animals don't wait for anybody, and I've stopped wanting them to.
lines.chat_missing: My first eagle lived with me twenty-two years. The one I've got now is good, but she doesn't know my voice the same way.
lines.chat_here: Nomads adjust, my father said. That's the whole profession. This world is only one more pasture, with different weather.
lines.tease_quiet: {name}, you're as quiet as my eagle, and she's very quiet. I like it, but I thought you should know.
lines.tease_talker: {name}, you've talked from one valley to the next. The sheep would have walked off long ago.
lines.tease_careful: {name}, you look at the ground longer than I do, and I'm old. Soon you'll be walking first.
lines.tease_bold: {name}, you run up a hill like a young horse. Young horses learn, and so will you.
lines.tease_any: {name}, you drink my tea and never bring sugar. One day I'll stop pouring it.
lines.tease_back: Ha, that's good, {name}. My sons used to talk to me like that, and I let them as well.
lines.take_it_kindly: That's true, {name}. I won't argue with something that's true.
lines.bristle: There's no need for that, {name}. I'd rather you spoke to me respectfully.
lines.apologise: I spoke badly, and I'm sorry for it. An old man should know better.
lines.double_down: I said it, and I'll say it again. An old man has earned that much.
lines.needle_quiet: You don't tell anybody what you see. On the pasture, a man who keeps quiet about wolves loses his herd.
lines.needle_talker: You talk so much that nothing out here will come near us. I can't read the ground through your noise.
lines.needle_careful: You wait and wait, and the weather turns while you're waiting. Some things don't let you take your time.
lines.needle_bold: You walk where I haven't walked yet. The ground lies, and one day it'll lie to you.
lines.needle_any: You don't watch where you put your feet. I've told you, and you don't listen.
lines.bite_back: I've walked this world longer than you've walked anything. Mind your own feet.
lines.hurt: I understand you. I'll walk on ahead for a while, then.
lines.laugh_off: My father said worse to me every day for thirty years. It didn't stop me then.
lines.confide: {name}, my sons didn't want the route, and I understood. It was still the end of six generations, and I carry that.
lines.listen: Sit, {name}, I'll pour more tea. Say as much as you want to, and no more.
lines.look_out: {name}, step where I step in there. The ground's bad, and I'd like to bring you out of it.
lines.accept: Thank you, {name}. I'll do as you say.
lines.deflect: An old herder has fallen off worse mountains, {name}. Don't worry about me.
lines.check_in: {name}, sit down and let me look properly. Where did it catch you?
lines.blame: Somebody stepped where I said not to. I saw it, and so did you.
lines.thank: I thought that was my last day. Thank you, and I'll pour your tea for a year.
lines.brush_off: It's nothing at all. You'd do the same for me, and I'd let you.
lines.worry: {name}, I saw you go down, and I'm too old for a fright like that. Sit with me a while.
lines.handed_down: I think you carried this before me. I'll keep it well until you want it back.
lines.hand_fine: Keep it, and use it well. An old man needs less than people think.
lines.hand_sulk: I'd have given it to you if you'd asked me. Nobody asked me.
lines.turn_friendly: {name}, you're always welcome at my tent. There'll always be tea for you.
lines.turn_friends: {name}, I'd walk the whole route with you, all three legs. I don't say that lightly.
lines.turn_grating: We don't walk at the same pace, you and I. It's better if I go ahead.
lines.turn_rivals: I'll walk first and you'll follow, because the ground needs it. That's all there'll be between us.
lines.make_up: Come and drink tea with me, {name}. I've been a stubborn old man, and we'll begin again.
lines.defend: That's not right, and you know it. Leave {name} alone, please.
lines.friend_left: The tent's quiet now {name} has gone home. There's nobody else to drink the tea.
lines.friend_back: {name}, you've come back. Good, the kettle's still warm.
lines.common_mountains: I spent forty summers on the high pasture, where the air's thin and the weather changes in an hour. Low ground still feels strange to me.
lines.common_birds: I hunted with golden eagles, like my father and his father. A bird that comes back to your glove is the best thing in the world.
lines.common_parent: I've got three sons in Bishkek and five grandchildren. I pray for all of them every evening, facing the mountains.
